headline: A 2012 executive order created a federal task force on commercial advocacy, meaning government efforts to support U.S. businesses competing for deals abroad.
what_it_does: The order set up a task force made up of several federal agencies. Based on the title, the group focuses on commercial advocacy, which usually means the government helping U.S. companies win business deals in other countries. No summary was provided, so details about the task force's members, duties, and powers are not available here.

who_it_affects.how: Agencies named in the order would take part in the new task force and coordinate their work on commercial advocacy.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. businesses seeking contracts or sales abroad
who_it_affects.how: These companies may get coordinated government support when competing for business overseas.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed December 6, 2012; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
